cards.front: not yet · meetings all day today · tomorrow first thing
cards.back: Todavía no, hoy he tenido reuniones todo el día.
cards.example: Te lo mando mañana a primera hora.
cards.translation: Hoy → perfecto in Spain: «he tenido». «Te lo mando» = present used as a promise. a primera hora = first thing.

cards.front: we've finalised the requirements · already started on the designs
cards.back: Hemos cerrado los requisitos.
cards.example: Y ya hemos empezado con los diseños.
cards.translation: Esta semana → perfecto. cerrar = to finalise (requirements, a deal, a topic). empezar con algo = to start on something.

cards.front: yes · this morning · they liked the proposal · want some changes
cards.back: Sí, he hablado con ellos esta mañana.
cards.example: Les ha gustado la propuesta, pero quieren algunos cambios.
cards.translation: Esta mañana (today) → perfecto: «he hablado», «les ha gustado». gustar works backwards: the proposal is the subject.

cards.context: ¿Le has mandado la presentación a Marta?
cards.front: yes · an hour ago · I've cc'd you
cards.back: Sí, se la he mandado hace una hora.
cards.translation: le + la → se la. Said the same day, Spain usually keeps the perfecto even with «hace una hora». poner a alguien en copia = to cc someone.

cards.context: ¿Has revisado ya los comentarios del equipo?
cards.front: not yet · didn't have time · this afternoon, without fail
cards.back: Todavía no, no me ha dado tiempo.
cards.example: Los miro esta tarde sin falta.
cards.translation: no me da tiempo = I don't have time (to do it), very common in Spain. Today → «no me ha dado tiempo». todavía no + perfecto = not yet.

cards.context: ¿Qué tal ha ido la reunión con dirección?
cards.front: better than I expected · they've approved our budget

fa.mejor de lo que esperaba: بهتر از چیزی که فکر می‌کردم

cards.back: Ha ido mejor de lo que esperaba.
cards.translation: ¿Qué tal ha ido…? / Ha ido bien = How did it go? (today) → perfecto. dirección = senior management.

cards.front: yes · we've decided to postpone it two weeks · more room
cards.back: Sí, hemos decidido aplazarlo dos semanas.
cards.translation: aplazar = to postpone. margen = room / buffer (time, budget).

cards.context: ¿Todo bien? Te veo un poco liado.
cards.front: non-stop since 8 today · can't keep up with everything
cards.back: Uf, hoy no he parado desde las ocho.
cards.example: No me ha dado la vida para todo.
cards.translation: Today → perfecto: «no he parado», «no me ha dado». no me da la vida = I can't keep up (very Spain). liado = busy.

cards.front: yes · they've sent the new screens · haven't been able to look yet
cards.back: Sí, han mandado las pantallas nuevas.
cards.example: Pero todavía no he podido verlas.
cards.translation: novedad = update / news (¿alguna novedad? = any updates?). todavía no + perfecto = not yet.

cards.front: intense · lots of firefighting · but good progress
cards.back: Intensa, hemos tenido que apagar muchos fuegos.
cards.translation: Esta semana → perfecto: «hemos tenido que», «hemos avanzado». apagar fuegos = firefighting (urgent problems).

cards.front: yes · waiting for legal's OK · can't move on until they reply
cards.back: Sí, estoy esperando el visto bueno de legal.
cards.example: Hasta que no contesten, no puedo avanzar.
cards.translation: hasta que + subjunctive (contesten) for something that hasn't happened yet; Spaniards often add «no»: «hasta que no contesten». el visto bueno = the OK.

cards.front: as soon as I have the data · I'll let you know · I reckon Thursday
cards.back: En cuanto tenga los datos, te aviso.
cards.translation: en cuanto + subjunctive (tenga): future events after en cuanto / cuando always take the subjunctive. calculo que… = I reckon…

cards.front: depends · the tests need to go well · if all goes well, yes
cards.back: Depende de que las pruebas salgan bien.
cards.translation: depender de que + subjunctive (salgan). But si + present: «si todo va bien» (never present subjunctive after si).

cards.front: you talk to the client · before they sign · it's the most urgent thing
cards.back: Necesito que hables con el cliente antes de que firmen.
cards.translation: necesitar que + subjunctive (hables). antes de que + subjunctive (firmen), always.

cards.front: very tight · if anything unexpected comes up, we won't make it
cards.back: Vamos muy justos.
cards.example: Como surja cualquier imprevisto, no llegamos.
cards.translation: como + subjunctive = if (as a warning): «como surja algo…». imprevisto = unexpected issue. llegar (a la fecha) = to make the deadline.

cards.front: stuck with the budget all morning · this afternoon I'll get onto it
cards.back: He estado toda la mañana atascado con el presupuesto.
cards.example: Esta tarde me pongo con el roadmap.
cards.translation: Toda la mañana (today) → perfecto: «he estado». atascado = stuck. ponerse con algo = to get going on something.

cards.context: ¿Quién se encarga del correo a los stakeholders?
cards.front: me · I'll send it once we've closed the dates
cards.back: Me encargo yo.
cards.example: Lo mando cuando hayamos cerrado las fechas.
cards.translation: encargarse de = to take care of. cuando + perfect subjunctive (hayamos cerrado) = once we have done it (future).

cards.front: I'd rather Laura did it · she knows the product better than me
cards.back: Preferiría que la presentara Laura.
cards.example: Conoce el producto mejor que yo.
cards.translation: Conditional (preferiría) + que → imperfect subjunctive (presentara). A polite way to say no.

cards.front: yes · we should talk it over before replying
cards.back: Sí, lo he visto.
cards.example: Conviene que lo hablemos antes de contestar.
cards.translation: conviene que + subjunctive (hablemos) = it's best that… (very common at work). antes de + infinitive when the subject doesn't change.

cards.context: ¿Qué tal vas de tiempo esta semana?
cards.front: flat out this week · if you could wait till Monday, that'd suit me great
cards.back: Esta semana voy a tope.
cards.example: Si pudieras esperar al lunes, me vendría genial.
cards.translation: Si + imperfect subjunctive (pudieras) + conditional (vendría) = a polite request. venir bien / genial = to suit.

cards.front: we were presenting · the system went down · nobody knew what to do
cards.back: Estábamos presentando cuando se cayó el sistema.
cards.translation: Estábamos presentando = background (imperfecto); se cayó = the event that interrupted it (indefinido). caerse = to go down (system, server).

cards.front: client changed the requirements halfway · we had to start almost from scratch
cards.back: El cliente cambió los requisitos a mitad de proyecto.
cards.example: Tuvimos que empezar casi de cero.
cards.translation: Finished events in a closed past → indefinido. a mitad de = halfway through.

cards.front: no · nobody had told us · we found out by chance
cards.back: No, nadie nos lo había dicho.
cards.translation: había dicho = pluperfect: it happened before another past moment. enterarse de = to find out (the everyday verb for it).

cards.front: that he'd send us the contract on Monday · still nothing
cards.back: Me dijo que nos mandaría el contrato el lunes.
cards.translation: Reported speech: «os mandaré el contrato» → «me dijo que nos mandaría el contrato» (future → conditional).

cards.front: I asked him to send it asap · we can't start without it
cards.back: Le pedí que lo mandara cuanto antes.
cards.translation: pedir que + subjunctive; with a past main verb (pedí) → imperfect subjunctive (mandara).

cards.front: we were reviewing the metrics · something didn't add up · that's when we noticed
cards.back: Estábamos revisando las métricas y algo no cuadraba.
cards.translation: Background (estábamos revisando, no cuadraba) → imperfecto; the moment you realised (nos dimos cuenta) → indefinido. cuadrar = to add up.

cards.context: ¿Al final se solucionó lo de ayer?
cards.front: yes · we fixed it in the afternoon · it was a configuration error
cards.back: Sí, lo arreglamos por la tarde.
cards.translation: lo de ayer / lo del cliente = the thing about… (very common). Yesterday → indefinido (arreglamos); era = description (imperfecto).

cards.front: I thought it would get fixed quickly · didn't want to worry anyone
cards.back: Pensaba que se solucionaría rápido.
cards.translation: Pensaba que + conditional (se solucionaría) = what you expected back then. No quería (imperfecto) for an intention, not quise.

cards.front: no · we hadn't had time · that was the problem
cards.back: No, no nos había dado tiempo.
cards.translation: Pluperfect (había dado) = before that past moment. «Ese fue el problema» → indefinido for a closed fact.

cards.context: ¿Qué sacamos en claro de todo esto?
cards.front: we should have tested more · next time, we'll do it differently
cards.back: Que tendríamos que haber probado más.
cards.example: La próxima vez lo haremos de otra manera.
cards.translation: tendría que haber + participle = should have (done), key for retros. sacar en claro = to take away (a lesson).

cards.front: makes sense to me · but I'd cut the scope a bit
cards.back: A mí me parece que tiene sentido.
cards.example: Pero yo recortaría un poco el alcance.
cards.translation: yo + conditional (recortaría) = a softened opinion or proposal. el alcance = the scope.

cards.context: Yo creo que deberíamos lanzar ya.
cards.front: I don't think it's a good idea · it isn't ready yet
cards.back: No creo que sea buena idea.
cards.translation: creo que + indicative, but NO creo que + subjunctive (sea). One of the most common triggers in meetings.

cards.context: ¿Y si lo dejamos para el próximo sprint?
cards.front: fine by me · as long as the client accepts it · we'd need to ask first
cards.back: Me parece bien, siempre que el cliente lo acepte.
cards.translation: siempre que + subjunctive (acepte) = as long as. habría que + infinitive = we'd need to (conditional of hay que).

cards.front: we prioritise the bugs · before adding new features
cards.back: Propongo que prioricemos los bugs.
cards.translation: proponer que + subjunctive (prioricemos; z → c before e). meter = to add / put in (colloquial). funcionalidad = feature.

cards.context: ¿Os parece bien hacer la reunión el jueves?
cards.front: Thursday is terrible for me · would Friday suit you all?
cards.back: El jueves me viene fatal.
cards.translation: venir bien / mal / fatal = to suit / not suit (times, dates). The conditional (vendría) makes the suggestion polite.

cards.front: almost · I'd like us to review the costs first · just in case
cards.back: Casi. Me gustaría que revisáramos los costes primero.
cards.translation: me gustaría que + imperfect subjunctive (revisáramos). costes (Spain) = costs.

cards.context: ¿Crees que el equipo puede con todo?
cards.front: honestly, I don't see it · unless they give us more people
cards.back: Sinceramente, no lo veo.
cards.example: A no ser que nos den más gente.
cards.translation: a no ser que + subjunctive (den) = unless. poder con algo = to be able to handle it. «No lo veo» = I don't see it happening.

cards.context: ¿Lo metemos en el roadmap de este trimestre?
cards.front: better to wait until we have the usage data · that way we decide with data
cards.back: Sería mejor esperar a que tengamos los datos de uso.
cards.translation: esperar a que + subjunctive (tengamos) = to wait until. sería mejor = it would be better.

cards.context: Me preocupa que no lleguemos a tiempo.
cards.front: if we'd started earlier, we wouldn't be in this situation · now we've got to push
cards.back: Si hubiéramos empezado antes, no estaríamos así.
cards.translation: Si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiéramos empezado) + conditional (estaríamos) = past condition, present result. toca + infinitive = it's time to.

cards.front: just one thing · it'd be good if someone sent a summary today · I can do it
cards.back: Solo una cosa: estaría bien que alguien mandara un resumen hoy.
cards.translation: estaría bien que + imperfect subjunctive (mandara) = it would be good if…, a polite way to propose a task.

cards.front: very quiet · didn't do much · I needed it
cards.back: Muy tranquilo, no he hecho gran cosa.
cards.translation: On Monday, Spaniards often talk about the weekend in the perfecto: «no he hecho gran cosa». hacer falta = to need. el finde = the weekend.

cards.front: no, never · they say it's beautiful · I'd love to go
cards.back: No, nunca he estado.
cards.example: Dicen que es precioso; me encantaría ir.
cards.translation: alguna vez / nunca + perfecto = life experience. me encantaría = I'd love to (conditional of encantar).

cards.front: two weeks in Portugal · we had a great time
cards.back: Estuvimos dos semanas en Portugal.
cards.translation: Finished holidays → indefinido (estuvimos). pasárselo genial / bien / fatal = to have a great / good / awful time.

cards.front: right on the beachfront · but the room was tiny
cards.back: Estaba en primera línea de playa.
cards.translation: Descriptions in the past → imperfecto (estaba, era). primera línea de playa = beachfront.

cards.front: depends on the weather · if it's nice, maybe the mountains
cards.back: Depende del tiempo que haga.
cards.example: Si hace bueno, igual me voy a la montaña.
cards.translation: depender de + el tiempo que / lo que + subjunctive (haga). el puente = long weekend around a public holiday. igual = maybe (colloquial Spain).

cards.context: ¿Qué tal te va en el nuevo puesto?
cards.front: it was quite hard at first · now I'm getting the hang of it
cards.back: Al principio me costó bastante.
cards.example: Pero ya le voy cogiendo el tranquillo.
cards.translation: Al principio + indefinido (me costó) = how it went at the start. ir + gerund (voy cogiendo) = gradual progress. costar = to be hard for someone.

cards.front: I'd love to · but I've got a call at 2 · another day?
cards.back: Me encantaría, pero tengo una llamada a las dos.
cards.translation: me encantaría = I'd love to (conditional = polite). dejar algo para otro día = to put it off. venirse = to come along.

cards.front: yes, finally · hope the weather's good · I really need to switch off
cards.back: Sí, por fin. Ojalá haga buen tiempo.
cards.translation: ojalá + present subjunctive (haga) = I hope. It comes from Arabic 'law šā' Allāh' (if God wills). hacer falta = to need.

cards.context: Me voy ya, que mañana tengo médico.
cards.front: OK · hope it goes well · see you Thursday
cards.back: Vale, que te vaya bien.
cards.translation: que + subjunctive = a wish: que te vaya bien, que descanses, que lo pases bien. Very common when saying goodbye.

cards.context: Si pudieras vivir en otra ciudad de España, ¿cuál elegirías?
cards.front: Valencia · for the sea and the weather · though I'd miss my friends here
cards.back: Elegiría Valencia, por el mar y el clima.
cards.example: Aunque echaría de menos a mis amigos de aquí.
cards.translation: Answer «si pudieras…, ¿qué harías?» with the conditional (elegiría, echaría). echar de menos = to miss (Spain).

cards.front: yes · yesterday · and called her again this morning · she agrees now
cards.back: Sí, hablé con ella ayer y esta mañana la he vuelto a llamar.
cards.translation: Same verb, two time frames: ayer → hablé (indefinido); esta mañana → he vuelto a llamar (perfecto). volver a + infinitive = to do again.

cards.front: Monday was chaos · since then, much better
cards.back: El lunes fue un caos.
cards.example: Pero desde entonces todo ha ido mucho mejor.
cards.translation: El lunes = a finished day → fue (indefinido). Desde entonces = from then until now → ha ido (perfecto).

cards.front: yes · sent it last Friday · no answer yet
cards.back: Sí, la envié el viernes pasado.
cards.translation: El viernes pasado → indefinido (envié). Todavía no = up to now → perfecto (han contestado).

cards.context: ¿Has estado alguna vez en la oficina de Barcelona?
cards.front: yes, twice · the last time was in March
cards.back: Sí, he estado dos veces.
cards.example: La última vez fue en marzo.
cards.translation: Life experience (alguna vez, dos veces) → perfecto. A specific time (en marzo) → indefinido.

cards.front: I joined two years ago · since then I've changed teams twice
cards.back: Entré hace dos años.
cards.example: Y desde entonces he cambiado de equipo dos veces.
cards.translation: Hace dos años → indefinido (entré). Desde entonces → perfecto (he cambiado). Also possible: «Llevo dos años en la empresa».

cards.context: ¿Qué tal ha ido hoy el taller con el cliente?
cards.front: really well · much better than last time · that time was a disaster
cards.back: Ha ido muy bien, mucho mejor que la última vez.
cards.translation: Hoy → ha ido (perfecto). Aquella vez = a finished occasion → fue (indefinido). taller = workshop.

cards.context: ¿Has visto el último informe de ventas?
cards.front: I skimmed it yesterday · haven't had time to analyse it yet
cards.back: Lo vi ayer por encima.
cards.example: Pero todavía no he tenido tiempo de analizarlo.
cards.translation: Ayer → vi. Todavía no → he tenido. por encima = quickly, without detail (to skim).

cards.front: he called me on Monday · nothing since then
cards.back: Me llamó el lunes.
cards.example: Y desde entonces no he sabido nada de él.
cards.translation: El lunes → llamó. Desde entonces (until now) → no he sabido nada. saber de alguien = to hear from someone.

cards.front: we've hit the targets · although July was very tough
cards.back: Hemos cumplido los objetivos.
cards.translation: The quarter that just ended still counts as 'now' → perfecto (hemos cumplido). July, a closed month → indefinido (fue). cumplir los objetivos = to hit the targets.

cards.front: yes · we met at a conference years ago · today I saw him again after ages
cards.back: Sí, nos conocimos en un congreso hace años.
cards.example: Y hoy lo he vuelto a ver después de mucho tiempo.
cards.translation: conocerse (indefinido) = to meet for the first time. Hoy → he vuelto a ver. congreso = conference (the event); conferencia = a talk.

cards.front: that he likes the idea · but wants to see numbers first
cards.back: Me ha dicho que le gusta la idea.
cards.example: Pero que antes quiere ver números.
cards.translation: Me ha dicho (today) → the reported verbs stay in the present. Repeating «que» before each idea is natural: «…pero que…».

cards.context: ¿Qué dijo Marta ayer en la reunión?
cards.front: that the project was going well · but they needed another developer
cards.back: Dijo que el proyecto iba bien.
cards.translation: Dijo (past) → present becomes imperfecto: «va bien» → iba bien, «necesitamos» → necesitaban.

cards.front: he told me yesterday he'd come later · he had a doctor's appointment
cards.back: Ayer me dijo que vendría más tarde.
cards.example: Que tenía cita en el médico.
cards.translation: Future → conditional when reported from the past: «vendré» → me dijo que vendría. tener cita (en el médico) = to have an appointment.

cards.front: whether we could deliver earlier · and how much it would cost
cards.back: Me preguntó si podíamos entregarlo antes.
cards.translation: Yes/no questions are reported with si. Question words keep their accent: cuánto, cuándo, cómo. «¿Cuánto costará?» → cuánto costaría.

cards.front: to review the document · before sending it to the client
cards.back: Me pidió que revisara el documento.
cards.translation: pedir que + subjunctive. After a past verb (pidió) → imperfect subjunctive: «revisa» → que revisara.

cards.front: we agreed to meet again next week · everyone brings a proposal
cards.back: Quedamos en vernos otra vez la semana que viene.
cards.example: Y cada uno traerá una propuesta.
cards.translation: quedar en + infinitive / quedar en que… = to agree on (very common in Spain). «¿En qué quedamos?» = so what did we agree?

cards.context: ¿Sabes si van a contratar a alguien?
cards.front: Laura mentioned yes · but she didn't know when
cards.back: Laura me comentó que sí.
cards.translation: comentar = to mention. «que sí / que no» = reported yes/no. «no sé» → no sabía.

cards.front: that they've approved it · but we'll have to cut ten percent
cards.back: Que nos lo han aprobado.
cards.example: Pero que tendremos que recortar un diez por ciento.
cards.translation: To answer «¿Qué ha dicho…?», start with «Que…». Reported today (ha dicho) → tenses don't change: tendremos.

cards.context: ¿Te dijo por qué se fue de la empresa?
cards.front: he said he'd been offered a better job · and fancied a change
cards.back: Me dijo que le habían hecho una oferta mejor.
cards.translation: Pluperfect (le habían hecho) = it happened before he told you. apetecer = to feel like / fancy.

cards.front: yes · they say they'll have it by Friday · but I wouldn't count on it
cards.back: Sí, dicen que lo tendrán para el viernes.
cards.example: Pero yo no contaría con ello.
cards.translation: dicen (present) → no tense change: lo tendrán. contar con algo = to count on something; the conditional softens it.

cards.context: Creo que deberíamos cancelar esta funcionalidad.
cards.front: I get your point · but I see it differently · users are asking for it
cards.back: Entiendo lo que dices, pero yo lo veo de otra manera.
cards.translation: Show you understand first, then disagree: «Entiendo lo que dices, pero…». la = la funcionalidad.

cards.context: El retraso es culpa del equipo técnico.
cards.front: I don't fully agree · the requirements changed several times too
cards.back: No estoy del todo de acuerdo.
cards.example: Los requisitos también cambiaron varias veces.
cards.translation: «no… del todo» softens disagreement. cambiaron = a closed series of past events (indefinido).

cards.front: you're partly right · but it's quite a bit more expensive to build
cards.back: En parte tienes razón.
cards.example: Pero es bastante más caro de desarrollar.
cards.translation: en parte = partly. caro / fácil / difícil de + infinitive = expensive / easy / hard to…

cards.context: Tenemos que lanzarlo este mes sí o sí.
cards.front: I find it a bit risky · what if we launch a beta first?
cards.back: Lo veo un poco arriesgado.
cards.translation: ¿Y si + present…? = what if…? (a soft proposal). sí o sí = no matter what. lo veo + adjective = I find it…

cards.front: OK · what we could do is offer more support hours · then the price stays

fa.lo que sí podríamos hacer es…: کاری که می‌تونیم بکنیم اینه که…

cards.back: Vale, pero lo que sí podríamos hacer es ofrecer más horas de soporte.
cards.translation: lo que (sí) podríamos hacer es… = a counter-proposal. tocar el precio = to change the price.

cards.front: I would · as long as they give us a fixed date · otherwise it makes no sense
cards.back: Yo aceptaría, siempre y cuando nos den una fecha cerrada.
cards.translation: siempre y cuando + subjunctive (den) = as long as. fecha cerrada = a fixed, confirmed date.

cards.front: it's not so much about money as about time · I'd ask for a longer deadline

fa.no es tanto una cuestión de dinero como: مسئله اونقدر پول نیست، بیشتر زمانه

cards.back: No es tanto una cuestión de dinero como de tiempo.
cards.translation: no es tanto X como Y = it's not so much X as Y. plazo = time allowed / deadline.

cards.context: Esto ya lo intentamos el año pasado y no funcionó.
cards.front: true · but back then we didn't have the data we have now
cards.back: Es verdad que no funcionó.
cards.example: Pero entonces no teníamos los datos que tenemos ahora.
cards.translation: El año pasado → no funcionó (indefinido). Entonces no teníamos → imperfecto, describing the situation back then.

cards.front: I'd rather we tested both options · and decided with data
cards.back: Preferiría que probáramos las dos opciones.
cards.translation: preferiría que + imperfect subjunctive (probáramos, decidiéramos).

cards.front: nearly there · let me check one detail with legal · I'll confirm tomorrow
cards.back: Ya casi lo tenemos. Déjame que consulte un detalle con legal.
cards.translation: déjame que + subjunctive (consulte) = let me… «Mañana te lo confirmo» = present used as a promise.

cards.front: it'd be great if you sent me the figures today · so I have time to prepare it
cards.back: Sería genial que me pasaras las cifras hoy.
cards.translation: sería genial / estaría bien que + imperfect subjunctive (pasaras). pasar = to send / share (files, figures).

cards.front: no need · it's already reviewed · thanks anyway
cards.back: No hace falta que lo revises, ya está revisado.
cards.translation: no hace falta que + subjunctive (revises) = there's no need for you to… gracias igualmente = thanks anyway.

cards.front: very complete · I'd just ask you to add a summary at the start
cards.back: Está muy completo.
cards.example: Solo te pediría que añadieras un resumen al principio.
cards.translation: Conditional (pediría) + imperfect subjunctive (añadieras) = soft, polite feedback.

cards.context: ¿Qué es lo más importante en este proyecto?
cards.front: that the client sees progress every week · otherwise they get nervous
cards.back: Lo más importante es que el cliente vea avances cada semana.
cards.translation: es importante / lo más importante es que + subjunctive (vea). ponerse nervioso = to get nervous.

cards.context: Voy a mandar el informe al cliente.
cards.front: before you send it, take a look at the numbers · last time an error slipped through

fa.se nos coló un error: یه اشتباه از زیر دستمون در رفت

cards.back: Antes de que lo mandes, échale un vistazo a los números.
cards.example: La última vez se nos coló un error.
cards.translation: antes de que + subjunctive, always (mandes). colarse un error = for an error to slip through. La última vez → indefinido (se coló).

cards.front: of course · as long as you leave everything ready · and let the team know
cards.back: Claro, siempre que lo dejes todo listo.
cards.translation: siempre que + subjunctive (dejes, avises) = as long as. cogerse un día libre = to take a day off (Spain).

cards.front: I'd like each person to present their part · five minutes max
cards.back: Me gustaría que cada uno presentara su parte.
cards.translation: ¿Cómo quieres que hagamos…? → present subjunctive after quieres que. Me gustaría que + imperfect subjunctive (presentara).

cards.context: Perdona, todavía no he terminado lo que me pediste.
cards.front: don't worry · send it to me when you can · no rush
cards.back: No te preocupes, mándamelo cuando puedas.
cards.translation: cuando + subjunctive for the future (puedas). no corre prisa = there's no rush.

cards.front: a lot · I'm glad you included the risks
cards.back: Me ha gustado mucho.
cards.example: Me alegra que hayas incluido los riesgos.
cards.translation: me alegra que + perfect subjunctive (hayas incluido) for something already done. Today → me ha gustado.

cards.context: Nadie ha actualizado el tablero esta semana.
cards.front: it's important we all update it before Friday's meeting · otherwise we don't know where we stand
cards.back: Es importante que todos lo actualicemos antes de la reunión del viernes.
cards.example: Si no, no sabemos cómo vamos.
cards.translation: es importante que + subjunctive (actualicemos). Including yourself (nosotros) sounds less bossy. ¿Cómo vamos? = how are we doing?

cards.context: …y por eso hay que migrar todo al nuevo sistema.
cards.front: sorry to interrupt · do you mean the whole platform?
cards.back: Perdona que te interrumpa.
cards.translation: perdona que + subjunctive (interrumpa) = sorry for (doing)… referirse a = to mean / refer to.

cards.context: ¿Me oyes? Se te corta un poco.
cards.front: sorry, my screen froze · can you repeat the last part?
cards.back: Perdona, se me ha congelado la pantalla.
cards.translation: se me ha congelado = it just happened to me (accidental se + perfecto). lo último = the last bit.

cards.context: ¿Por qué no te convence la propuesta?
cards.front: well · it's not that I don't like it · it's that it's too expensive
cards.back: A ver, no es que no me guste.
cards.translation: no es que + subjunctive (guste), es que + indicative (es) = it's not that…, it's that… «A ver» buys you time to think.

cards.front: no · what I mean is we should postpone it · I mean, not cancel it completely
cards.back: No, lo que quiero decir es que deberíamos aplazarlo.
cards.example: O sea, no cancelarlo del todo.
cards.translation: lo que quiero decir es que… = what I mean is… o sea = I mean / in other words.

cards.front: by the way · going back to what Marta said earlier · it's worth reviewing
cards.back: Por cierto, volviendo a lo que ha dicho Marta antes…
cards.example: Creo que merece la pena revisarlo.
cards.translation: por cierto = by the way. volviendo a… = going back to… ha dicho (earlier in this meeting) → perfecto.

cards.front: hmm · good question · let me check and I'll tell you
cards.back: Pues… buena pregunta.
cards.example: Déjame que lo mire y te digo.
cards.translation: Pues… = well… (buys time). déjame que + subjunctive (mire). «y te digo» = and I'll let you know.

cards.front: long story short · in the end we got three new clients · not bad at all
cards.back: Total, que al final conseguimos tres clientes nuevos.
cards.translation: Total, que… = long story short (to wrap up a story). A finished event → conseguimos (indefinido).

cards.context: Creo que eso no es lo que acordamos.
cards.front: you're right · I explained myself badly · I meant next month, not this one
cards.back: Tienes razón, me he explicado mal.
cards.example: Quería decir el mes que viene, no este.
cards.translation: Just now → me he explicado mal (perfecto). «Quería decir» and «quise decir» both mean 'I meant'.

cards.front: yes · to sum up: Marta handles the budget and I talk to the client · see you Thursday?
cards.back: Sí. Resumiendo: Marta se encarga del presupuesto y yo hablo con el cliente.
cards.translation: Resumiendo / en resumen = to sum up. The present works for agreed plans (yo hablo, nos vemos).

cards.front: honestly · I haven't thought about it enough · can I tell you tomorrow?
cards.back: La verdad es que no lo he pensado lo suficiente.
cards.translation: la verdad es que… = honestly / the thing is… (very frequent). lo suficiente = enough. ¿Te lo digo mañana? = present for an offer.

cards.front: I went to the doctor yesterday
cards.back: Fui al médico ayer
cards.example: Y me dijo que todo iba mejor.
cards.translation: ir → fui. Indefinido because it is a completed event in a closed past period.

cards.front: I was at home all day
cards.back: Estuve en casa todo el día
cards.translation: estar → estuve. Indefinido because the state is treated as a completed block of time.

cards.front: I had a stressful meeting
cards.back: Tuve una reunión estresante
cards.translation: tener → tuve. Important irregular 'uve' family.

cards.front: I got a lot done yesterday
cards.back: Ayer hice un montón de cosas
cards.example: Por eso hoy estoy tan cansado.
cards.translation: hacer → hice. Irregular in every person: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. Ayer = finished time → indefinido. If it's still today, Spain uses the perfecto: «Hoy he hecho un montón de cosas».

cards.front: I couldn't sleep last night
cards.back: No pude dormir anoche
cards.translation: poder → pude. Completed inability in a closed past period.

cards.front: I didn't mean that
cards.back: No quise decir eso
cards.translation: querer → quise. «No quise decir eso» = I didn't mean that; «quise decir…» = I meant… In the affirmative, quise + infinitive = I tried to. For 'I wanted to (but didn't)', use quería or iba a: «Te iba a llamar, pero se me hizo tarde». If it just happened: «me he expresado mal».

cards.front: The doctor told me to rest
cards.back: El médico me dijo que descansara
cards.translation: decir → dijo. Indirect recommendation triggers subjuntivo.

cards.front: I put the book on the table
cards.back: Puse el libro en la mesa
cards.example: Y luego me fui a dormir.
cards.translation: poner → puse. Important 'use' family irregular.

cards.front: I got home late
cards.back: Llegué tarde a casa
cards.translation: llegar → llegué (g → gu before e). For 'got home / arrived', Spanish uses llegar. Use venir only for coming to where you are right now.

cards.front: I brought the documents
cards.back: Traje los documentos
cards.translation: traer → traje. Same irregular family as decir/dije.

cards.front: I knew it from the moment I saw him
cards.back: Lo supe desde el momento en que lo vi
cards.translation: saber → supe = the moment you knew or found out. Careful: the exclamation 'I knew it!' is «¡Lo sabía!» (imperfecto).

cards.front: I met an interesting guy
cards.back: Conocí a un tío interesante
cards.translation: conocer → conocí. In indefinido often means meeting someone for the first time. In Spain a «conferencia» is a talk; the event is a «congreso» or «evento».

cards.front: I drove to Madrid
cards.back: Conduje hasta Madrid
cards.translation: conducir → conduje. '-ducir' verbs follow the same irregular pattern.

cards.front: They brought me good news
cards.back: Me trajeron buenas noticias
cards.example: Y me quedé mucho más tranquilo.
cards.translation: traer → trajeron. Third person plural irregular.

cards.front: They told me the results were good
cards.back: Me dijeron que los resultados eran buenos
cards.translation: decir → dijeron. Notice the dropped 'i' in dijeron.

cards.front: I was able to finish the book
cards.back: Pude terminar el libro
cards.translation: poder → pude. Completed successful action.

cards.front: I wanted to change jobs, but I decided to wait
cards.back: Quería cambiar de trabajo, pero decidí esperar
cards.translation: Quería = what you wanted (background, imperfecto). Decidí = what actually happened (indefinido). Don't use quise for 'I wanted to (but didn't)': quise means you actually tried.

cards.front: I had to explain everything
cards.back: Tuve que explicar todo
cards.translation: tener que + infinitive = had to do something.

cards.front: I came because I was worried
cards.back: Vine porque estaba preocupado
cards.translation: Mix of indefinido event + imperfecto emotional background.

cards.front: I put on a new shirt
cards.back: Me puse una camisa nueva
cards.translation: ponerse → me puse. Very common reflexive irregular.

cards.front: I found out yesterday
cards.back: Lo supe ayer
cards.translation: saber → supe = found out. Even more common in speech: «Me enteré ayer». quedarse de piedra = to be stunned.

cards.front: I said the same thing
cards.back: Dije lo mismo
cards.translation: decir → dije. Very high-frequency irregular.

cards.front: I brought coffee for everyone
cards.back: Traje café para todos
cards.example: Porque la reunión iba a ser larga.
cards.translation: traer → traje. Extremely useful social/work verb.

cards.front: I was with friends all evening
cards.back: Estuve con amigos toda la tarde
cards.translation: Completed social time block in the past.

cards.front: I did what I could
cards.back: Hice lo que pude
cards.translation: Very common natural Spanish chunk.

cards.front: I came to learn Spanish
cards.back: Vine para aprender español
cards.example: Y al final me quedé aquí.
cards.translation: Movement verb + purpose structure.

cards.front: I put too much pressure on myself
cards.back: Me puse demasiada presión
cards.translation: Natural emotional usage of ponerse. Also very common in Spain: «meterse presión» — «No te metas tanta presión».

cards.front: I had a weird feeling
cards.back: Tuve una sensación rara
cards.translation: Tuve = a feeling at one specific moment. For an ongoing feeling, use the imperfecto: «Tenía una sensación rara desde por la mañana».

cards.front: I couldn't concentrate
cards.back: No pude concentrarme
cards.example: Tenía demasiadas cosas en la cabeza.
cards.translation: Very useful emotional/work chunk.

cards.front: I went out for beers with friends
cards.back: Fui de cañas con amigos
cards.translation: Classic Spain social expression.

cards.front: I went straight home after work
cards.back: Fui directamente a casa después del trabajo
cards.example: No tenía energía para nada más.
cards.translation: ir → fui. Completed movement/action in a closed time period.

cards.front: I was there for almost three hours
cards.back: Estuve allí casi tres horas
cards.translation: estar → estuve. Duration treated as a completed block.

cards.front: I had a long conversation with my mentor
cards.back: Tuve una conversación larga con mi mentor
cards.translation: tener → tuve. Common professional/social structure.

cards.front: I did everything they asked me
cards.back: Hice todo lo que me pidieron
cards.example: Pero aun así no fue suficiente.
cards.translation: hacer → hice. Very common real-life chunk.

cards.front: I couldn't stop thinking about it
cards.back: No pude dejar de pensar en eso
cards.translation: poder → pude. Completed inability.

cards.front: I wanted to explain it better
cards.back: Quise explicarlo mejor
cards.translation: querer → quise = I tried to (and it didn't go well). Compare: «quería explicarlo mejor» = I wanted to (just the wish).

cards.front: I said something stupid
cards.back: Dije una tontería
cards.translation: decir → dije. High-frequency conversational verb.

cards.front: I put my phone on silent mode
cards.back: Puse el móvil en silencio
cards.translation: poner → puse. Everyday practical usage.

cards.front: I came in early yesterday
cards.back: Ayer vine pronto
cards.translation: venir → vine: say it when you're at that place now (e.g. at the office). Pronto = early (very common in Spain). For this morning, Spain uses the perfecto: «Esta mañana he venido pronto».

cards.front: I brought my laptop with me
cards.back: Traje el portátil conmigo
cards.translation: traer → traje. Very useful professional chunk.

cards.front: I found out too late
cards.back: Lo supe demasiado tarde
cards.example: Y ya no pude hacer nada.
cards.translation: saber → supe often means discovering information suddenly.

cards.front: I met her through work
cards.back: La conocí por el trabajo
cards.translation: conocer in indefinido = meeting someone for the first time.

cards.front: I drove for six hours
cards.back: Conduje durante seis horas
cards.translation: conducir → conduje. Irregular '-je' family.

cards.front: They brought more documents
cards.back: Trajeron más documentos
cards.translation: traer → trajeron. Third person plural irregular.

cards.front: They told me to stay calm
cards.back: Me dijeron que me calmara
cards.translation: Indirect speech + subjunctive.

cards.front: I was able to relax a bit
cards.back: Pude relajarme un poco
cards.example: Después de hablar con el médico.
cards.translation: Completed successful action.

cards.front: I wanted to tell you earlier
cards.back: Te lo quería decir antes
cards.translation: Quería = an intention that didn't happen (imperfecto), not quise. Natural word order: «Te lo quería decir antes».

cards.front: I had to cancel the meeting
cards.back: Tuve que cancelar la reunión
cards.translation: tener que = obligation in the past.

cards.front: I came to support my wife
cards.back: Vine para apoyar a mi mujer
cards.translation: venir + para + infinitive = purpose structure.

cards.front: I put too much pressure on the team
cards.back: Le metí demasiada presión al equipo
cards.translation: meterle presión a alguien = to put pressure on someone (colloquial Spain). meter → metí.

cards.front: I had a terrible headache
cards.back: Tuve un dolor de cabeza horrible
cards.translation: Very common health-related chunk.

cards.front: I couldn't understand what happened
cards.back: No pude entender lo que pasó
cards.translation: poder → pude. Closed completed inability.

cards.front: I went for a walk to clear my mind
cards.back: Fui a dar un paseo para despejarme
cards.translation: Very natural Spain Spanish chunk.

cards.front: I was at the hospital all morning yesterday
cards.back: Ayer estuve en el hospital toda la mañana
cards.translation: estar → estuve. Ayer → indefinido. If it was today, Spain uses the perfecto: «Hoy he estado en el hospital toda la mañana».

cards.front: I had the feeling that something was wrong
cards.back: Tuve la sensación de que algo iba mal
cards.translation: Mix of indefinido event + imperfecto background.

cards.front: I did my best
cards.back: Hice lo mejor que pude
cards.translation: Extremely useful conversational structure.

cards.front: I couldn't find the words
cards.back: No pude encontrar las palabras
cards.translation: Very useful emotional communication chunk. Also very natural: «No me salían las palabras».

cards.front: I said exactly the same thing
cards.back: Dije exactamente lo mismo
cards.translation: hacer caso = to pay attention/listen.

cards.front: I brought everything I needed
cards.back: Traje todo lo que necesitaba
cards.translation: Useful preparation/planning context.

cards.front: I came back much calmer
cards.back: Volví mucho más tranquilo
cards.example: Después de hablar con el especialista.
cards.translation: volver → volví = came back. Venir only means coming to where you are right now.

cards.front: I put all my energy into learning
cards.back: Puse toda mi energía en aprender
cards.example: Y empecé a notar los resultados.
cards.translation: Natural motivational/progress expression.

cards.front: I had a really productive week
cards.back: Tuve una semana muy productiva
cards.translation: tener + period of time = very common structure. Talking about this week (not over yet), Spain uses the perfecto: «He tenido una semana muy productiva».

cards.front: I couldn't answer immediately
cards.back: No pude responder inmediatamente
cards.translation: Professional/workplace chunk.

cards.front: I wanted to change many things at once
cards.back: Quise cambiar demasiadas cosas a la vez
cards.translation: quise + infinitive = I tried to. Natural emotional reflection structure.

cards.front: I said it without thinking
cards.back: Lo dije sin pensar
cards.translation: Very high-frequency conversational chunk.

cards.front: I went through a difficult period
cards.back: Pasé por una etapa difícil
cards.translation: pasar por = to go through emotionally.

cards.front: I had no choice
cards.back: No tuve otra opción
cards.translation: Classic high-frequency structure. Colloquial Spain: «No me quedó otra».

cards.front: I couldn't handle everything
cards.back: No pude con todo
cards.translation: poder con algo = to handle/manage something.

cards.front: I built up too many expectations
cards.back: Me hice demasiadas expectativas
cards.translation: hacerse expectativas = to build up expectations (hacer → hice → me hice). Similar: «me puse el listón muy alto» = I set the bar too high.

cards.front: I came to Spain to start over
cards.back: Vine a España para empezar de nuevo
cards.translation: Strong emotional life-story structure. Spanish prefers «me cambió la vida» to «cambió mi vida».

cards.front: I brought up the topic during dinner
cards.back: Saqué el tema durante la cena
cards.example: Y todos se quedaron en silencio.
cards.translation: sacar un tema = to bring up a topic.

cards.front: I realized too late
cards.back: Me di cuenta demasiado tarde
cards.translation: darse cuenta = to realize. One of the most important Spanish chunks.

cards.front: I became obsessed with the problem
cards.back: Me obsesioné con el problema
cards.translation: Reflexive emotional verb in indefinido.

cards.front: I got really nervous
cards.back: Me puse muy nervioso
cards.translation: ponerse = to become/change state.

cards.front: I suddenly felt much better
cards.back: De repente me sentí mucho mejor
cards.example: Como si me hubiera quitado un peso de encima.
cards.translation: sentirse in indefinido = emotional change at a specific moment. como si + hubiera + participle = as if (something) had happened.

cards.front: I ended up completely exhausted
cards.back: Terminé completamente agotado
cards.translation: terminar + adjective = ending up in a state.

cards.front: I spent the whole weekend studying
cards.back: Pasé todo el fin de semana estudiando
cards.translation: pasar + time + gerund = spending time doing something.

cards.front: I finally understood everything
cards.back: Por fin entendí todo
cards.translation: entender in indefinido = moment of comprehension.

cards.front: I forgot to reply
cards.back: Se me olvidó responder
cards.example: Tenía demasiadas cosas en la cabeza.
cards.translation: Very common accidental structure in Spanish.

cards.front: I felt a huge relief
cards.back: Sentí un alivio enorme
cards.translation: sentir in indefinido = specific emotional reaction.

cards.front: I tried to stay calm
cards.back: Intenté mantener la calma
cards.translation: intentar = to try. Very high-frequency emotional/work verb.

cards.front: I decided to take a break
cards.back: Decidí tomarme un descanso
cards.translation: decidir = to decide. tomarse un descanso = to take a break.

cards.front: I finally managed to finish it
cards.back: Por fin conseguí terminarlo
cards.translation: conseguir = to manage/achieve successfully.

cards.front: I forgot the meeting completely
cards.back: Olvidé la reunión por completo
cards.example: Tenía demasiadas cosas en la cabeza.
cards.translation: olvidar = to forget. Even more natural in speech: «Se me olvidó la reunión por completo».

cards.front: I suddenly remembered something important
cards.back: De repente me acordé de algo importante
cards.example: Y tuve que volver a casa.
cards.translation: acordarse de = to remember.

cards.front: I noticed that she was worried
cards.back: Noté que estaba preocupada
cards.translation: notar = to notice/perceive emotionally.

cards.front: I changed my mind
cards.back: Cambié de opinión
cards.translation: Very common conversational chunk.

cards.front: I left my laptop at home
cards.back: Me dejé el portátil en casa
cards.example: Y me di cuenta demasiado tarde.
cards.translation: dejarse algo = to leave something behind by accident. Very common in Spain: «Me he dejado las llaves».

cards.front: I kept thinking about it all day
cards.back: Seguí pensando en eso todo el día
cards.translation: seguir + gerund = to keep doing something.

cards.front: I started feeling much better
cards.back: Empecé a sentirme mucho mejor
cards.translation: empezar a + infinitive = to start doing something.

cards.front: I ended up really liking Madrid
cards.back: Al final Madrid me acabó gustando mucho
cards.translation: acabar + gerund = to end up doing/feeling something. With gustar: «me acabó gustando».

cards.front: I helped a friend with his project
cards.back: Ayudé a un amigo con su proyecto
cards.translation: ayudar = very common social/professional verb.

cards.front: I avoided talking about the topic
cards.back: Evité hablar del tema
cards.translation: evitar = to avoid.

cards.front: I organized everything last night
cards.back: Organicé todo anoche
cards.example: Para no ir con prisas hoy.
cards.translation: organizar = very useful productivity verb.

cards.front: I prepared for the interview all week
cards.back: Me preparé para la entrevista toda la semana
cards.translation: prepararse para = prepare oneself for.

cards.front: I reviewed the document several times
cards.back: Revisé el documento varias veces
cards.translation: revisar = review/check carefully.

cards.front: I fixed the problem yesterday afternoon
cards.back: Ayer por la tarde arreglé el problema
cards.translation: arreglar = fix/solve. Ayer → indefinido. Said the same day, Spain uses the perfecto: «Esta mañana he arreglado el problema».

cards.front: I took advantage of the free time
cards.back: Aproveché el tiempo libre
cards.example: Y avancé bastante con el libro.
cards.translation: aprovechar = to make good use of.

cards.front: I improved a lot last month
cards.back: El mes pasado mejoré muchísimo
cards.translation: mejorar = improve. El mes pasado → indefinido. Este mes (still running) → «Este mes he mejorado muchísimo».

cards.front: I got really stressed again
cards.back: Volví a estresarme muchísimo
cards.translation: volver a + infinitive = to do something again (very common). Spanish avoids «mi estrés empeoró»; it says «volví a estresarme».

cards.front: I trusted him immediately
cards.back: Confié en él inmediatamente
cards.translation: confiar en = to trust.

cards.front: I supported my wife during a difficult period
cards.back: Apoyé a mi mujer durante una etapa difícil
cards.example: Y ella hizo lo mismo conmigo.
cards.translation: apoyar = emotional/social support verb.

cards.front: We argued about work again
cards.back: Discutimos otra vez sobre el trabajo
cards.translation: discutir = to argue/discuss intensely. Also natural: «Volvimos a discutir por el trabajo».

cards.front: I relaxed a bit last weekend
cards.back: El fin de semana pasado me relajé un poco
cards.translation: relajarse = emotional recovery verb. El fin de semana pasado → indefinido. On Monday, many Spaniards say «Este fin de semana me he relajado».

cards.front: I got excited about the opportunity
cards.back: Me ilusioné con la oportunidad
cards.translation: ilusionarse = to become excited/hopeful.

cards.front: I realized what the real problem was
cards.back: Me di cuenta de cuál era el verdadero problema
cards.example: Y todo empezó a tener sentido.
cards.translation: darse cuenta de = to realize.

cards.front: The situation turned out better than expected
cards.back: La situación resultó mejor de lo esperado
cards.example: Y me quedé mucho más tranquilo.
cards.translation: resultar = to turn out/result.

cards.front: The meeting seemed endless
cards.back: La reunión parecía interminable
cards.translation: parecer = to seem/appear.

cards.front: I gradually got used to the rhythm
cards.back: Poco a poco me acostumbré al ritmo
cards.translation: acostumbrarse a = to get used to.

cards.front: I continued learning even when I was tired
cards.back: Seguí aprendiendo incluso cuando estaba cansado
cards.translation: seguir + gerund = to keep doing something.

cards.front: I changed a lot of habits last year
cards.back: El año pasado cambié muchos hábitos
cards.example: Y ahora me siento mejor mentalmente.
cards.translation: El año pasado → indefinido. Este año (still running) → «Este año he cambiado muchos hábitos».

cards.front: I tried to explain it clearly
cards.back: Intenté explicarlo claramente
cards.translation: Very useful work communication chunk.

cards.front: I managed to disconnect for a while
cards.back: Conseguí desconectar un rato
cards.translation: desconectar = mentally disconnect/unwind.

cards.front: I started taking things more calmly
cards.back: Empecé a tomarme las cosas con más calma
cards.translation: tomarse las cosas con calma = important emotional chunk.

cards.front: I ended up understanding his point
cards.back: Acabé entendiendo su punto de vista
cards.example: Aunque al principio no estaba de acuerdo.
cards.translation: acabar + gerund = eventual realization.

cards.front: I helped organize the event
cards.back: Ayudé a organizar el evento
cards.translation: Combination of social + productivity verbs.

cards.front: I avoided checking my phone constantly
cards.back: Evité mirar el móvil constantemente
cards.translation: Very modern daily-life chunk.

cards.front: I prepared everything in advance
cards.back: Preparé todo con antelación
cards.translation: con antelación = beforehand/in advance.

cards.front: I reviewed my notes before the meeting
cards.back: Revisé mis apuntes antes de la reunión
cards.translation: apuntes = notes.

cards.front: I fixed things with my friend
cards.back: Arreglé las cosas con mi amigo
cards.example: Y ahora estamos bien otra vez.
cards.translation: arreglar las cosas = repair a relationship/problem.

cards.front: I took advantage of the quiet atmosphere
cards.back: Aproveché el ambiente tranquilo
cards.translation: ambiente = atmosphere/vibe.

cards.front: I improved little by little
cards.back: Mejoré poco a poco
cards.translation: poco a poco = gradually.

cards.front: Things got worse after the meeting
cards.back: Las cosas empeoraron después de la reunión
cards.example: Había mucha tensión en el equipo.
cards.translation: empeorar often used impersonally with situations.

cards.front: I trusted my instincts
cards.back: Confié en mis instintos
cards.translation: instintos = instincts.

cards.front: I supported him emotionally
cards.back: Lo apoyé emocionalmente
cards.example: Estaba pasando por un momento duro.
cards.translation: pasar por un momento duro = go through a hard moment.

cards.front: We discussed the problem calmly
cards.back: Discutimos el problema con calma
cards.translation: discutir doesn't always mean aggressive argument.

cards.front: I relaxed after hearing the news
cards.back: Me relajé después de escuchar la noticia
cards.translation: respirar tranquilo = breathe relieved.

cards.front: I got excited again about learning Spanish
cards.back: Me ilusioné otra vez con aprender español
cards.translation: Very useful motivation/emotional-learning chunk.

cards.front: I realized I needed balance
cards.back: Me di cuenta de que necesitaba equilibrio
cards.translation: Important reflective structure.

cards.front: Everything turned out fine in the end
cards.back: Al final todo resultó bien
cards.translation: Natural closure phrase. Even more common in speech: «Al final todo salió bien».

cards.front: I was thinking about changing jobs
cards.front example: When suddenly another company called me.
cards.back: Estaba pensando en cambiar de trabajo
cards.example: Cuando de repente me llamaron de otra empresa.
cards.translation: Imperfecto gives the background action; indefinido introduces the event that interrupts it. pensar en = to think about.

cards.front: I was having dinner when he called me
cards.front example: I wasn't expecting the call at all.
cards.back: Estaba cenando cuando me llamó
cards.example: No me esperaba la llamada para nada.
cards.translation: Estaba cenando = ongoing background; me llamó = completed interrupting event.

cards.front: I didn't understand what was happening
cards.front example: Everything happened too fast.
cards.back: No entendía qué estaba pasando
cards.translation: Imperfecto describes the ongoing state of not understanding; ocurrió marks the completed event.

cards.front: I was feeling a bit strange that day
cards.front example: I didn't know exactly why.
cards.back: Ese día me sentía un poco raro
cards.translation: Sentirse in imperfecto describes an ongoing emotional state.

cards.front: I thought everything was going well
cards.front example: But then I received some unexpected news.
cards.back: Pensaba que todo iba bien
cards.example: Pero luego recibí una noticia inesperada.
cards.translation: Pensaba + iba = two imperfectos describing a past belief and the background situation.

cards.front: I was about to leave when she arrived
cards.front example: So I stayed a little longer.
cards.back: Estaba a punto de irme cuando llegó
cards.example: Así que me quedé un rato más.
cards.translation: Estar a punto de + infinitive = to be about to do something.

cards.front: I used to work from home
cards.front example: And I had quite a lot of flexibility.
cards.back: Trabajaba desde casa
cards.translation: Imperfecto expresses a repeated or habitual past situation.

cards.front: I used to go there every Friday
cards.front example: But I haven't been there for months.
cards.back: Iba allí todos los viernes
cards.example: Pero hace meses que no voy.
cards.translation: Ir → iba. Imperfecto is natural with repeated past habits.

cards.front: Before, I didn't understand this
cards.front example: Now it seems much clearer to me.
cards.back: Antes no entendía esto
cards.example: Ahora me resulta mucho más claro.
cards.translation: Antes + imperfecto describes a past state that has changed.

cards.front: I was trying to explain the situation
cards.front example: But nobody seemed to be listening to me.
cards.back: Estaba intentando explicar la situación
cards.translation: Estaba intentando = ongoing attempt. intentar + infinitive = to try to do something.

cards.front: Nobody seemed to understand
cards.front example: So I had to explain it again.
cards.back: Nadie parecía entenderlo
cards.example: Así que tuve que explicarlo otra vez.
cards.translation: Parecer = to seem. Tuve que = I had to, a completed past obligation.

cards.front: I didn't know what to say
cards.front example: My mind went completely blank.
cards.back: No sabía qué decir
cards.translation: Saber → sabía. No sabía qué decir is a very common conversational pattern.

cards.front: I was worried about what might happen
cards.front example: But I tried not to think about it too much.
cards.back: Me preocupaba lo que pudiera pasar
cards.example: Pero intenté no darle demasiadas vueltas.
cards.translation: Me preocupaba works like gustar: «lo que pudiera pasar» is the subject. pudiera = imperfect subjunctive. darle vueltas a algo = to overthink something.

cards.front: I kept telling myself that everything would be fine
cards.front example: Even though I was quite nervous inside.
cards.back: Me repetía que todo saldría bien
cards.example: Aunque por dentro estaba bastante nervioso.
cards.translation: Me repetía = repeated background action. Saldría = conditional for future viewed from a past perspective.

cards.front: I didn't expect it to happen so quickly
cards.front example: It completely caught me by surprise.
cards.back: No esperaba que ocurriera tan rápido
cards.translation: No esperaba = imperfecto for an expectation at that time. ocurriera = imperfect subjunctive of ocurrir, needed after «no esperaba que».

cards.front: I was getting used to the new routine
cards.front example: At first it was quite difficult for me.
cards.back: Me estaba acostumbrando a la nueva rutina
cards.translation: Estar + gerund expresses an ongoing process. acostumbrarse a = to get used to.

cards.front: At first, everything felt strange
cards.front example: But little by little I adapted to the new situation.
cards.back: Al principio todo resultaba extraño
cards.example: Pero poco a poco me fui adaptando.
cards.translation: Resultar = to seem/turn out. adaptarse = to adapt.

cards.front: I was slowly getting better
cards.front example: And I started to get my confidence back.
cards.back: Poco a poco iba mejorando
cards.example: Y empecé a recuperar la confianza.
cards.translation: Ir + gerund emphasizes gradual progression. recuperar = to recover/regain.

cards.front: I didn't realize how tired I was
cards.front example: Until I got home.
cards.back: No me daba cuenta de lo cansado que estaba
cards.translation: Darse cuenta in imperfecto describes an ongoing lack of awareness; llegué marks the specific moment.

cards.front: When I arrived, everyone was already eating
cards.front example: So I sat down with them.
cards.back: Cuando llegué, todos ya estaban comiendo
cards.example: Así que me senté con ellos.
cards.translation: Llegué = completed event; estaban comiendo = ongoing background action.

cards.front: I wanted to leave, but I stayed
cards.front example: In the end, the conversation became interesting.
cards.back: Quería irme, pero me quedé
cards.example: Al final la conversación se puso interesante.
cards.translation: Quería = intention/background state; me quedé = completed decision/action.

cards.front: I felt more confident after that
cards.front example: And I started speaking more easily.
cards.back: Después de eso me sentí más seguro
cards.example: Y empecé a hablar con más soltura.
cards.translation: Sentirse in indefinido marks a change in emotional state. con soltura = fluently/naturally.

cards.front: I realized I was overthinking everything
cards.front example: And I decided to stop doing it so much.
cards.back: Me di cuenta de que estaba dándole demasiadas vueltas a todo
cards.translation: Me di cuenta = completed realization; estaba dándole vueltas = ongoing mental process.

cards.front: I was looking for a solution
cards.front example: When suddenly an idea came to me.
cards.back: Estaba buscando una solución
cards.example: Cuando se me ocurrió una idea.
cards.translation: Estaba buscando = background action. ocurrírsele algo a alguien = for an idea to occur to someone.

cards.front: I suddenly had an idea
cards.front example: And everything started to make sense.
cards.back: De repente se me ocurrió una idea
cards.translation: Ocurrírsele algo a alguien = to suddenly think of/have an idea. encajar = to fit/make sense.

cards.front: I was expecting something different
cards.front example: But reality was different.
cards.back: Me esperaba algo diferente
cards.translation: Esperarse algo = to expect something. The reflexive form is very common in conversation.

cards.front: I didn't feel like going out
cards.front example: I preferred to stay at home.
cards.back: No me apetecía salir
cards.translation: Apetecer = to feel like/want to do something. Very useful Spain Spanish verb.

cards.front: I felt like having a coffee
cards.front example: So I went to a café.
cards.back: Me apetecía tomar un café
cards.example: Así que fui a una cafetería.
cards.translation: Me apetecía = I felt like having. Apetecer is normally used with an indirect-object structure.

cards.front: I was enjoying the evening
cards.front example: When it started raining.
cards.back: Estaba disfrutando de la noche
cards.translation: Estaba disfrutando = ongoing action interrupted by empezó.

cards.front: We were having a great time
cards.front example: Until we had to leave.
cards.back: Nos lo estábamos pasando genial
cards.translation: Pasárselo genial = to have a great time. Very natural conversational Spanish.

cards.front: I was talking to a friend when I got the news
cards.front example: It really surprised me.
cards.back: Estaba hablando con un amigo cuando me enteré de la noticia
cards.translation: Estaba hablando = background; me enteré = completed discovery. enterarse de = to find out.

cards.front: I had been thinking about it for days
cards.front example: But I still hadn't made a decision.
cards.back: Llevaba días pensando en ello
cards.example: Pero todavía no había tomado una decisión.
cards.translation: Llevar + time + gerund = to have been doing something for a period of time.

cards.front: I was feeling more and more comfortable speaking Spanish
cards.front example: And that really encouraged me.
cards.back: Cada vez me sentía más cómodo hablando español
cards.translation: Imperfecto for an ongoing change. cada vez + más/menos = more and more / less and less. animar = to encourage.

cards.front: I was afraid of making a mistake
cards.front example: But I worried about it less and less.
cards.back: Tenía miedo de equivocarme
cards.example: Pero cada vez me preocupaba menos.
cards.translation: Tener miedo de + infinitive = to be afraid of doing something. cada vez menos = less and less.

cards.front: I didn't want to interrupt you
cards.front example: So I waited until you finished speaking.
cards.back: No quería interrumpirte
cards.example: Por eso esperé a que terminaras.
cards.translation: Quería = imperfecto because it describes intention at that moment. esperar a que + subjunctive is required.

cards.front: I was wondering if you could help me
cards.front example: It's a fairly quick thing.
cards.back: Me preguntaba si podrías ayudarme
cards.translation: Me preguntaba = softens a request. podrías = conditional for politeness.

cards.front: I thought you were going to come
cards.front example: That's why I didn't message you.
cards.back: Pensaba que ibas a venir
cards.translation: Pensaba = past belief; ibas a venir = near/future-in-the-past construction.

cards.front: I was going to call you
cards.front example: But it got very late.
cards.back: Iba a llamarte
cards.translation: Ir a + infinitive in imperfecto expresses an intended future action from a past perspective. hacerse tarde = to get late.

cards.front: I was having a bad day
cards.front example: And everything was annoying me.
cards.back: Estaba teniendo un mal día
cards.translation: Imperfecto describes the ongoing background of the day. «un mal día» (adjective first) is the natural chunk. molestar = to bother/annoy.

cards.front: Everything was going according to plan
cards.front example: Until a problem came up.
cards.back: Todo iba según lo previsto
cards.translation: Ir = to go/progress. surgir = to arise/come up.

cards.front: Then an unexpected problem came up
cards.front example: And we had to change our plans.
cards.back: Entonces surgió un problema inesperado
cards.example: Y tuvimos que cambiar de planes.
cards.translation: Surgir = to arise. Indefinido marks the new event in the story.

cards.front: We had to change our plans
cards.front example: But in the end everything went well.
cards.back: Tuvimos que cambiar de planes
cards.example: Pero al final salió todo bien.
cards.translation: Tuvimos que = completed past obligation. cambiar de planes = change plans.

cards.front: In the end, everything worked out
cards.front example: Although at first things looked pretty bad.
cards.back: Al final todo salió bien
cards.example: Aunque al principio pintaba bastante mal.
cards.translation: Salir bien = to work out well. Pintar mal = to look bad/not look promising.

cards.front: At first it looked complicated
cards.front example: But once I got the hang of it, it became easier.
cards.back: Al principio parecía complicado
cards.example: Pero cuando le cogí el tranquillo, se volvió más fácil.
cards.translation: Parecía = background impression. parecer = to seem.

cards.front: Once I got the hang of it, it became easier
cards.front example: I no longer had to think about it so much.
cards.back: Cuando le cogí el tranquillo, se volvió más fácil
cards.example: Ya no tenía que pensar tanto.
cards.translation: Cogerle el tranquillo a algo = to get the hang of it. Very useful colloquial expression.

cards.front: I was slowly getting the hang of it
cards.front example: And it came out more and more naturally.
cards.back: Poco a poco le iba cogiendo el tranquillo
cards.example: Y cada vez me salía con más naturalidad.
cards.translation: Iba + gerund emphasizes gradual progress. cada vez + más = more and more. salir con naturalidad = come out naturally.

cards.front: I felt like I was making progress
cards.front example: And that gave me quite a lot of motivation.
cards.back: Sentía que estaba avanzando
cards.example: Y eso me daba bastante motivación.
cards.translation: Sentía = ongoing perception; estaba avanzando = ongoing progress.

cards.front: I finally realized what I had been doing wrong
cards.front example: And since then I've tried to avoid it.
cards.back: Por fin me di cuenta de lo que estaba haciendo mal
cards.translation: Completed realization + imperfect progressive action. desde entonces = since then.

cards.front: I was making the same mistake over and over
cards.front example: Until someone pointed it out to me.
cards.back: Cometía el mismo error una y otra vez
cards.example: Hasta que alguien me lo señaló.
cards.translation: Imperfecto for repeated past behavior. señalar = to point something out.

cards.front: I'll deal with it tomorrow
cards.front example: Today I need to switch off.
cards.back: Mañana me encargaré de ello
cards.translation: Future for a future intention. encargarse de = to take care of/deal with.

cards.front: I'll let you know
cards.front example: As soon as I have any news.
cards.back: Te avisaré
cards.translation: Avisar = to let someone know/inform someone. Very useful everyday verb.

cards.front: I'll keep you updated
cards.front example: If anything changes, I'll let you know.
cards.back: Te mantendré al tanto
cards.translation: Mantener al tanto = to keep someone informed. Natural professional/social phrase.

cards.front: I'll probably stay home tonight
cards.front example: I'm pretty tired.
cards.back: Probablemente me quedaré en casa esta noche
cards.translation: Future expresses a prediction/intention. quedarse = to stay.

cards.front: He'll probably be at work
cards.front example: That's why he's not answering.
cards.back: Estará trabajando
cards.translation: Future can express present probability: estará = he is probably.

cards.front: That must be expensive
cards.front example: It looks like it costs quite a lot.
cards.back: Eso será caro
cards.translation: Future probability is very common in Spanish for guesses about the present. tener pinta de = look/seem likely to.

cards.front: What time will you arrive?
cards.front example: Let me know when you're nearby.
cards.back: ¿A qué hora llegarás?
cards.translation: Future for asking about a future event. In everyday speech the present is more common: «¿A qué hora llegas?». cuando + future reference takes the present subjunctive (estés).

cards.front: I'll see what I can do
cards.front example: But I don't promise anything.
cards.back: Veré qué puedo hacer
cards.translation: Veré = I will see. Useful when you cannot promise a result.

cards.front: I'll try to sort it out
cards.front example: And I'll tell you as soon as I know more.
cards.back: Intentaré solucionarlo
cards.example: Y te cuento algo en cuanto sepa más.
cards.translation: Intentaré = future of intentar. solucionar = to solve/fix an issue.

cards.front: I'll probably need more time
cards.front example: I don't want to do it in a rush.
cards.back: Probablemente necesitaré más tiempo
cards.translation: Future prediction + necesitar = to need. con prisas = in a rush.

cards.front: Could you give me a hand?
cards.front example: I only have one more thing left to finish.
cards.back: ¿Podrías echarme una mano?
cards.example: Solo me queda una cosa por terminar.
cards.translation: Conditional for polite requests. echar una mano = to give a hand/help.

cards.front: Would you mind waiting a moment?
cards.front example: I have to finish this first.
cards.back: ¿Te importaría esperar un momento?
cards.translation: Te importaría = very polite conditional request. importar = to mind.

cards.front: I would like to ask you something
cards.front example: It's a slightly sensitive topic.
cards.back: Me gustaría preguntarte una cosa
cards.example: Es un tema un poco delicado.
cards.translation: Me gustaría = I would like. Conditional gives politeness and softens the request.

cards.front: I'd rather stay at home
cards.front example: I don't feel like going out today.
cards.back: Preferiría quedarme en casa
cards.translation: Preferiría = I would rather. Conditional expresses preference politely.

cards.front: I would probably do the same
cards.front example: I don't see many alternatives.
cards.back: Probablemente haría lo mismo
cards.translation: Conditional expresses a hypothetical reaction. alternativa = alternative.

cards.front: I wouldn't do that if I were you
cards.front example: But obviously it's your decision.
cards.back: Yo no haría eso si fuera tú
cards.translation: Classic hypothetical: conditional + imperfect subjunctive. fuera = imperfect subjunctive of ser.

cards.front: If I had more time, I'd travel more
cards.front example: But right now I don't have much time.
cards.back: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más
cards.example: Pero ahora mismo voy bastante justo.
cards.translation: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional = hypothetical present situation. ir justo de tiempo = have little time.

cards.front: If I could, I'd take a few days off
cards.front example: I need to switch off for a bit.
cards.back: Si pudiera, me tomaría unos días libres
cards.translation: Pudiera = imperfect subjunctive; me tomaría = conditional. tomarse días libres = take days off.

cards.front: If I were you, I'd talk to her first
cards.front example: That way you could avoid misunderstandings.
cards.back: Yo que tú, hablaría con ella primero
cards.translation: «Yo que tú» + conditional = the most common way to give advice in Spain (= si yo fuera tú). malentendido = misunderstanding.

cards.front: I'd be happier if I had more free time
cards.front example: I've been extremely busy lately.
cards.back: Sería más feliz si tuviera más tiempo libre
cards.translation: Conditional expresses the hypothetical result; imperfect subjunctive expresses the hypothetical condition. ir a tope = be extremely busy.

cards.front: I would have done it differently
cards.front example: But at that time I didn't have all the information.
cards.back: Lo habría hecho de otra manera
cards.example: Pero en aquel momento no tenía toda la información.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect = habría + participle. Used for hypothetical actions in the past.

cards.front: I would have called you, but I didn't have your number
cards.front example: I remembered too late.
cards.back: Te habría llamado, pero no tenía tu número
cards.translation: Habría llamado = unrealized past action. Imperfecto describes the background reason.

cards.front: I should probably reconsider it
cards.front example: There are some factors I hadn't considered.
cards.back: Probablemente debería replanteármelo
cards.example: Hay algunos factores que no había considerado.
cards.translation: Debería = conditional of deber, often used for advice or soft self-recommendation. replanteárselo = reconsider it.

cards.front: You should give it another thought
cards.front example: You don't have to decide today.
cards.back: Deberías pensártelo otra vez
cards.translation: Deberías = soft advice. pensárselo = to think something over.

cards.front: It would be better to wait
cards.front example: That way we'll have more information.
cards.back: Sería mejor esperar
cards.translation: Sería mejor = it would be better. Conditional softens advice.

cards.front: It wouldn't hurt to ask
cards.front example: Worst case, they'll say no.
cards.back: No estaría de más preguntar
cards.example: Como mucho, te dirán que no.
cards.translation: No estaría de más = it wouldn't hurt / it wouldn't be a bad idea. Very useful idiomatic phrase.

cards.front: Maybe we should postpone it
cards.front example: We don't have enough time right now.
cards.back: Quizá deberíamos aplazarlo
cards.example: Ahora mismo no tenemos tiempo suficiente.
cards.translation: Deberíamos = conditional advice. aplazar = postpone.

cards.front: I'd suggest talking to your manager
cards.front example: Maybe they can give you a hand.
cards.back: Yo sugeriría hablar con tu jefe
cards.translation: Sugeriría = conditional makes the suggestion less forceful. echar una mano = help.

cards.front: I'd avoid making a decision right now
cards.front example: I'd wait until I had more information.
cards.back: Yo evitaría tomar una decisión ahora mismo
cards.translation: Evitaría = I would avoid. Conditional expresses cautious advice.

cards.front: I'd take the opportunity if I were you
cards.front example: Opportunities like this don't come along very often.
cards.back: Yo aprovecharía la oportunidad si fuera tú
cards.translation: Aprovechar = make use of/take advantage of. Hypothetical advice structure.

cards.front: I might go if the weather improves
cards.front example: We'll see what happens tomorrow.
cards.back: Igual voy si mejora el tiempo
cards.translation: Igual + present can mean 'maybe/perhaps' in colloquial Spain Spanish.

cards.front: Maybe I'll join you later
cards.front example: It depends on how the afternoon goes.
cards.back: Igual me uno a vosotros más tarde
cards.example: Depende de cómo vaya la tarde.
cards.translation: Igual = maybe/perhaps in colloquial Spain. unirse = to join.

cards.front: I'll probably have finished by then
cards.front example: So we can meet without any problem.
cards.back: Para entonces probablemente ya habré terminado
cards.example: Así que podremos quedar sin problema.
cards.translation: Future perfect = habré + participle. Used for an action completed before a future point.

cards.front: By next month, I'll have finished the course
cards.front example: After that I want to start another one.
cards.back: Para el mes que viene habré terminado el curso
cards.translation: Future perfect emphasizes completion before a future deadline. ponerse con = start working on.

cards.front: By the time you arrive, I'll already have left
cards.front example: But I'll leave the keys for you.
cards.back: Cuando llegues, ya me habré ido
cards.translation: Me habré ido = future perfect of irse. When referring to the future, Spanish uses subjunctive after cuando.

cards.front: I would have finished earlier if I hadn't been interrupted
cards.front example: I lost almost an hour because of that.
cards.back: Habría terminado antes si no me hubieran interrumpido
cards.example: Perdí casi una hora con eso.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect + pluperfect subjunctive = unreal past condition and result.

cards.front: I would have accepted if the conditions had been different
cards.front example: But it wasn't worth it for me.
cards.back: Habría aceptado si las condiciones hubieran sido diferentes
cards.translation: Past hypothetical. compensar = to be worth it/pay off.

cards.front: What would you do in my situation?
cards.front example: I need an honest opinion.
cards.back: ¿Qué harías tú en mi situación?
cards.translation: Conditional is used for hypothetical questions and advice.

cards.front: What would you have done?
cards.front example: I want to know how you would have approached it.
cards.back: ¿Qué habrías hecho tú?
cards.example: Quiero saber cómo lo habrías planteado.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect asks about an alternative past action. plantear = approach/frame a problem.

cards.front: I would never have imagined that
cards.front example: A few years ago, it would have seemed impossible to me.
cards.back: Nunca me habría imaginado eso
cards.example: Hace unos años me habría parecido imposible.
cards.translation: Habría imaginado = unrealized past perspective. Useful for expressing surprise.

cards.front: A few years ago, I would have found this impossible
cards.front example: And now it's part of my everyday life.
cards.back: Hace unos años me habría parecido imposible
cards.example: Y ahora forma parte de mi día a día.
cards.translation: Habría parecido = conditional perfect for a hypothetical past perspective.

cards.front: I think I'll need to rethink my approach
cards.front example: Some things aren't working.
cards.back: Creo que tendré que replantearme el enfoque
cards.example: Hay cosas que no están funcionando.
cards.translation: Tendré que = I will have to. replantearse = reconsider/rethink; enfoque = approach.

cards.front: I'll probably end up changing my mind
cards.front example: The same thing always happens to me.
cards.back: Probablemente acabaré cambiando de opinión
cards.translation: Acabar + gerund in future = will end up doing something.

cards.front: I wouldn't rule it out
cards.front example: But I wouldn't get my hopes up either.
cards.back: No lo descartaría
cards.example: Pero tampoco me haría muchas ilusiones.
cards.translation: Descartar = rule out/discard. Conditional softens the statement.

cards.front: I wouldn't get my hopes up
cards.front example: Until we have something confirmed.
cards.back: No me haría muchas ilusiones
cards.translation: Hacerse ilusiones = get one's hopes up. Very natural emotional expression.

cards.front: That would make a huge difference
cards.front example: Especially in the long term.
cards.back: Eso supondría una gran diferencia
cards.translation: Suponer = mean/represent/entail. Conditional is useful for hypothetical consequences.

cards.front: It would be worth it
cards.front example: If it really helps you make progress.
cards.back: Merecería la pena
cards.example: Si realmente te ayuda a avanzar.
cards.translation: Merecer la pena = to be worth it. Conditional expresses hypothetical value.

cards.front: ¡Qué va!
cards.back: Colloquial expression used to strongly but casually say 'no' or deny something.
