cards.translation: Very common in Spain. Means something like 'not at all'.

cards.front: Vaya
cards.back: Expression of surprise, disappointment, admiration, or reaction depending on tone.
cards.example: Vaya, no me esperaba esa noticia.
cards.translation: A very versatile Spanish reaction word.

cards.front: Nunca mejor dicho
cards.back: Used when a phrase fits perfectly in the context, often humorously.
cards.example: Hace un frío que pela y me he quedado helado… nunca mejor dicho.
cards.translation: Literally: 'never better said'. Used when an expression is literally true in the situation.

cards.front: Da gusto
cards.back: Expression used when something feels pleasant or satisfying.
cards.translation: Means something like 'it's a pleasure'.

cards.front: Buen rollo
cards.back: Good vibes, positive atmosphere.
cards.example: Hay muy buen rollo entre nosotros.
cards.translation: Opposite: mal rollo.

cards.front: Mal rollo
cards.back: Bad atmosphere, tension, uncomfortable feeling.
cards.example: Ese sitio me dio mal rollo.
cards.translation: Very common colloquial expression.

cards.front: De por medio
cards.back: Something involved or influencing the situation.
cards.example: Cuando hay dinero de por medio, todo se complica.
cards.translation: Often used for emotions, problems, money, relationships, etc.

cards.front: Echar un ojo
cards.back: To take a look at something.
cards.example: ¿Le puedes echar un ojo a estos resultados?
cards.translation: Very common informal expression.

cards.front: Te lo mereces
cards.back: You deserve it.
cards.example: Después de todo el esfuerzo, te lo mereces.
cards.translation: Used for encouragement or recognition.

cards.front: Momentito
cards.back: Diminutive of 'momento'; sounds softer and affectionate.
cards.example: Un momentito, que termino esto y estoy contigo.
cards.translation: Spanish often uses diminutives for emotional tone.

cards.front: Anda
cards.back: Colloquial expression used to encourage, soften, or react.
cards.translation: Does not mean 'walk' in these contexts.

cards.front: Me ha dejado loco
cards.back: Something surprised or shocked me strongly.
cards.example: La noticia me ha dejado loco.
cards.translation: Very colloquial.

cards.front: Ya te pillo
cards.back: I get you / I see what you mean.
cards.example: —¿Entiendes lo que quiero decir? —Sí, sí, ya te pillo.
cards.translation: Careful: «¡Te he pillado!» means 'Gotcha! I caught you'.

cards.front: No complicarse la vida
cards.back: To keep things simple; not to make things harder than they need to be.
cards.example: No te compliques la vida: mándale un correo y ya está.
cards.translation: Very common advice in Spain. «Y ya está» = and that's it.

cards.front: De buen rollo
cards.back: In a friendly way, with no bad intentions.
cards.example: Te lo digo de buen rollo, ¿eh?
cards.translation: Softens feedback or a comment so it doesn't sound like criticism. Very useful at work.

cards.front: Lástima
cards.back: What a pity.
cards.translation: Soft way to express disappointment.

cards.front: Planazo
cards.back: A really great plan.
cards.example: Ir de cervezas con amigos es un planazo.
cards.translation: -azo adds emphasis.

cards.front: Vas volando
cards.back: You are progressing very fast.
cards.example: Ya has terminado cinco capítulos, vas volando.
cards.translation: Literally: 'you're flying'.

cards.front: Ya tocaba
cards.back: It was about time.
cards.translation: From the verb tocar = to correspond/be the moment.

cards.front: Soler
cards.back: Verb used for habits or things that usually happen.
cards.example: La gente suele tomar café por la mañana.
cards.translation: Structure: soler + infinitive.

cards.front: Suena bien
cards.back: It sounds good.
cards.translation: Sonar often means 'to seem/sound'.

cards.front: Repasar
cards.back: To review or refresh knowledge.
cards.translation: Not learning from zero.

cards.front: Profundizar en
cards.back: To deepen knowledge about something.
cards.translation: Always used with 'en'.

cards.front: Certificación
cards.back: The certification process or achievement.
cards.example: Estoy preparando una certificación de AWS.
cards.translation: The achievement/title.

cards.front: Certificado
cards.back: The actual document proving something.
cards.translation: The physical/digital proof.

cards.front: Significado
cards.back: Meaning of a word or phrase.
cards.translation: Most common everyday word.

cards.front: Significación
cards.back: Formal or academic meaning/interpretation.
cards.example: La significación del símbolo es profunda.
cards.translation: Used in linguistics or formal analysis.

cards.front: Rollo
cards.back: Vibe, atmosphere, feeling.
cards.translation: Very colloquial Spanish word. Also: «¡Qué rollo!» = how boring!

cards.front: He estado tomando
cards.back: Present perfect continuous; emphasizes ongoing/recent process.
cards.example: He estado tomando pastillas estos meses.
cards.translation: Focuses on duration/process.

cards.front: He tomado
cards.back: Present perfect; focuses on completed action/result.
cards.translation: More neutral and factual.

cards.front: Le pedí que me diera
cards.back: Example of imperfect subjunctive after pedir que.
cards.example: Le pedí que me diera una baja médica.
cards.translation: Structure: pedir que + subjuntivo.

cards.front: Me recetó
cards.back: Past tense of recetar; used for doctors prescribing medicine.
cards.translation: Very common in medical contexts.

cards.front: Derivarme a cardiología
cards.back: To refer/send someone to a medical specialist.
cards.example: Quería saber si podían derivarme a cardiología.
cards.translation: Formal medical wording.

cards.front: Palpitaciones
cards.back: Heart palpitations.
cards.translation: Medical vocabulary.

cards.front: Sala de espera
cards.back: Waiting room.
cards.example: Estoy en la sala de espera.
cards.translation: Common hospital vocabulary.

cards.front: Espirometría
cards.back: Spirometry test.
cards.example: Ya me he hecho la espirometría.
cards.translation: Medical vocabulary.

cards.front: Me quedo tranquilo
cards.back: I feel relieved/reassured.
cards.translation: Very common emotional expression.

cards.front: Qué tal
cards.back: How are things?/How's it going?
cards.translation: Very common greeting.

cards.front: Cuánto tiempo
cards.back: Long time no see.
cards.translation: Used for reunions.

cards.front: trapista ❌ → terapeuta ✅
cards.back: A 'terapeuta' is a therapist or psychologist. 'Trapista' sounds like a Trappist monk.
cards.example: Tuve una sesión con mi terapeuta.
cards.translation: Similar words: psicólogo, terapeuta.

cards.front: me lo merezco
cards.back: Expression meaning 'I deserve it'. Uses reflexive verb merecerse.
cards.example: Después de esta semana, me lo merezco.
cards.translation: Related: te lo mereces, se lo merece.

cards.front: ordenar la casa
cards.back: To tidy or organize the house.
cards.example: Hoy me toca ordenar un poco la casa.
cards.translation: Similar: limpiar la casa, recoger.

cards.front: dar una baja médica
cards.back: Expression used when a doctor grants medical leave.
cards.example: La médica me dio una semana de baja.
cards.translation: Related: estar de baja, coger una baja.

cards.front: aprovechar para
cards.back: To use an opportunity or free time for something useful.
cards.example: Estoy aprovechando esta semana para estudiar.
cards.translation: Similar: sacar provecho, utilizar el tiempo.

cards.front: dar señales de vida
cards.back: To contact someone after a while or show that you are still around.
cards.translation: Related: aparecer otra vez, volver a escribir.

cards.front: tener mil cosas en la cabeza
cards.back: To have too many things on your mind.
cards.example: Perdona, es que tengo mil cosas en la cabeza.
cards.translation: Similar: tener la cabeza hecha un lío (= to be all confused).

cards.front: aclararse (las ideas)
cards.back: To get your thoughts straight; to figure things out.
cards.example: Necesitaba unos días para aclararme las ideas.
cards.translation: Very common: «No me aclaro» = I can't figure it out / I'm confused.

cards.front: despejarse
cards.back: To clear one's mind or relax mentally.
cards.example: Salir a caminar me ayuda a despejarme.
cards.translation: Similar: relajarse, desconectar.

cards.front: desconectar
cards.back: To mentally disconnect from stress or work.
cards.example: Necesito desconectar este fin de semana.
cards.translation: Related: relajarse, tomarse un respiro.

cards.front: tomarse un respiro
cards.back: To take a break and breathe mentally/emotionally.
cards.example: Después de tanto estrés, necesito tomarme un respiro.
cards.translation: Similar: descansar un poco, desconectar.

cards.front: ir al grano
cards.back: To get to the point directly.
cards.translation: Related: ser directo, no andarse con rodeos.

cards.front: darle vueltas a algo
cards.back: To overthink something; to keep turning it over in your head.
cards.translation: Not the same as «andarse con rodeos» (to beat around the bush).

cards.front: pillar algo
cards.back: To understand something.
cards.translation: Similar: entender, captar.

cards.front: captar
cards.back: To grasp or understand an idea.
cards.example: No capté la broma al principio.
cards.translation: Related: pillar, entender.

cards.front: liado
cards.back: Busy, overwhelmed, occupied.
cards.example: He estado muy liado estos días.
cards.translation: Similar: ocupado, saturado.

cards.front: saturado
cards.back: Mentally overloaded.
cards.translation: Related: agobiado, sobrecargado.

cards.front: agobiado
cards.back: Feeling overwhelmed or emotionally pressured.
cards.translation: Similar: saturado, estresado.

cards.front: currar
cards.back: Informal verb meaning 'to work'.
cards.example: Hoy me toca currar todo el día.
cards.translation: Formal version: trabajar.

cards.front: plan tranquilo
cards.back: A calm, relaxed plan.
cards.translation: Opposite: plan movido, fiesta.

cards.front: tomar algo
cards.back: To go out for a drink or snack socially.
cards.translation: Related: ir de cañas, tomar una cerveza.

cards.front: ir de cañas
cards.back: To go out for beers/tapas.
cards.translation: Related: tomar algo, ir a tomar una cerveza.

cards.front: me hace ilusión
cards.back: Expression for being happy/excited about something.
cards.example: Me hace ilusión verte otra vez.
cards.translation: Similar: me alegra, me entusiasma.

cards.front: caer bien
cards.back: To like someone / someone gives a good impression.
cards.example: Tu amigo me cae muy bien.
cards.translation: Opposite: caer mal.

cards.front: caer mal
cards.back: To dislike someone / someone gives a bad impression.
cards.translation: Opposite: caer bien.

cards.front: estar desaparecido
cards.back: To have been out of touch for a while (often said jokingly).
cards.example: Perdona, he estado desaparecido estas semanas.
cards.translation: Related: dar señales de vida = to get back in touch.

cards.front: estar a tope con algo
cards.back: To be fully focused on / extremely busy with something.
cards.example: Esta semana estoy a tope con la certificación.
cards.translation: Also: ir a tope = to be flat out. Similar: estar liado.

cards.front: suena a
cards.back: Expression meaning 'it seems like'.
cards.example: Eso suena a una muy buena idea.
cards.translation: Related: parece, da la impresión.

cards.front: andar con cuidado
cards.back: To be careful.
cards.translation: Similar: tener cuidado, ir con ojo.

cards.front: ir con ojo
cards.back: To stay alert or cautious.
cards.example: Ve con ojo con ese contrato.
cards.translation: Related: tener cuidado, estar atento.

cards.front: Hostia
cards.back: Literal meaning: the communion wafer in Catholicism. Real usage: a very common exclamation for surprise, shock, admiration, anger, etc.
cards.translation: Very Spanish. Tone completely changes meaning.

cards.front: Joder
cards.back: Literal meaning: to fuck/have sex (vulgar). Real usage: used constantly as 'damn', 'fuck', 'seriously', etc.
cards.translation: One of the most common emotional words in Spain.

cards.front: Qué fuerte
cards.back: Literal meaning: how strong. Real usage: something shocking, intense, unbelievable or emotionally impactful.
cards.translation: Very common reaction phrase.

cards.front: Flipar
cards.back: Literal meaning: to hallucinate/trip. Real usage: to be amazed, shocked or blown away.
cards.translation: Originally linked to drug culture decades ago.

cards.front: Rayarse
cards.back: Literal meaning: to scratch/make lines. Real usage: to overthink, obsess or mentally spiral.
cards.example: No te rayes tanto por eso.
cards.translation: Mental stress vocabulary in Spain.

cards.front: Ni de coña
cards.back: Literal meaning: not even joking. Real usage: absolutely no way.
cards.translation: Strong informal refusal.

cards.front: De puta madre
cards.back: Literal meaning: of prostitute mother. Real usage: amazing, excellent, fantastic.
cards.example: La cena estuvo de puta madre.
cards.translation: Very vulgar literally, but extremely common positively.

cards.front: Coño
cards.back: Literal meaning: vagina/cunt (vulgar). Real usage: emotional exclamation similar to 'damn', 'come on', 'shit'.
cards.translation: Very contextual. Friends use it constantly.

cards.front: Anda ya
cards.back: Literal meaning: go/walk already. Real usage: no way, come on, I don't believe you.
cards.translation: Can be playful disbelief.

cards.front: Madre mía
cards.back: Literal meaning: my mother. Real usage: expression of surprise, stress, admiration or exhaustion.
cards.translation: Safe and universal expression.

cards.front: Tela
cards.back: Literal meaning: fabric/cloth. Real usage: something intense, excessive or difficult.
cards.translation: Spain-specific metaphorical use.

cards.front: Tiene tela
cards.back: Literal meaning: it has fabric. Real usage: this situation is crazy/complicated/ridiculous.
cards.translation: Usually judgmental or dramatic.

cards.front: En plan
cards.back: Literal meaning: in plan/in style. Real usage: filler word like English 'like'.
cards.example: Y yo en plan: ¿qué está pasando?
cards.translation: Young people use it nonstop.

cards.front: Ya ves
cards.back: Literal meaning: now you see. Real usage: exactly, that's life, totally.
cards.translation: Agreement/resignation expression.

cards.front: Tal cual
cards.back: Literal meaning: such which/exactly as. Real usage: exactly, literally true.
cards.translation: Very common modern phrase.

cards.front: Qué cabrón
cards.back: Literal meaning: what a bastard/goat-like man. Real usage: can mean asshole OR lucky/funny bastard among friends.
cards.example: Te dieron vacaciones extra, qué cabrón.
cards.translation: Dangerous phrase if tone is wrong.

cards.front: Mazo
cards.back: Literal meaning: mallet/hammer. Real usage: very/a lot.
cards.translation: Classic Madrid slang.

cards.front: Tío
cards.back: Literal meaning: uncle. Real usage: dude/guy/man.
cards.translation: Probably the most common social word in Spain.

cards.front: Tronco
cards.back: Literal meaning: tree trunk. Real usage: dude/bro.
cards.translation: Very Madrid/street style, and a bit dated: «tío» is far more common today.

cards.front: Currárselo
cards.back: Literal meaning: to work it for oneself. Real usage: to put effort into something.
cards.translation: Implies respect for effort.

cards.front: Estar hasta los huevos
cards.back: Literal meaning: to be up to the eggs/testicles. Real usage: to be fed up.
cards.example: Estoy hasta los huevos del estrés.
cards.translation: Extremely common vulgar phrase.

cards.front: Acojonado
cards.back: Literal meaning: with big balls/testicle-related fear. Real usage: terrified or very nervous.
cards.translation: Very colloquial emotional word.

cards.front: Cojonudo
cards.back: Literal meaning: testicle-related. Real usage: excellent, awesome.
cards.translation: Funny positive vulgarity.

cards.front: La hostia
cards.back: Literal meaning: the communion wafer. Real usage: incredible, intense, crazy good/bad.
cards.translation: Can express admiration or intensity.

cards.front: Me cago en...
cards.back: Literal meaning: I shit on... Real usage: strong frustration expression.
cards.example: Me cago en todo, he perdido el móvil.
cards.translation: Very Spanish swearing structure.

cards.front: Paso
cards.back: Literal meaning: I pass. Real usage: I don't want to bother / I'm not interested.
cards.translation: Short casual refusal.

cards.front: Molar
cards.back: Literal meaning: no literal modern meaning. Real usage: to be cool.
cards.translation: Essential colloquial Spain verb.

cards.front: Petarlo
cards.back: Literal meaning: to explode/break something. Real usage: to crush it, become hugely successful.
cards.translation: Popular modern slang.

cards.front: Estar petado
cards.back: Literal meaning: exploded/burst. Real usage: crowded, packed or exhausted.
cards.translation: Depends heavily on context.

cards.front: Estar hecho polvo
cards.back: Literal meaning: to be made into dust. Real usage: physically or emotionally exhausted.
cards.translation: Very visual metaphor.

cards.front: Montárselo bien
cards.back: Literal meaning: to assemble/set it up well for oneself. Real usage: to enjoy life/have a great time.
cards.example: Se lo montan bien los fines de semana.
cards.translation: Can imply partying or simply enjoying life.

cards.front: Qué pasada
cards.back: Literal meaning: what a passing. Real usage: amazing, incredible.
cards.translation: Strong positive admiration.

cards.front: Menuda movida
cards.back: Literal meaning: what a movement. Real usage: what a mess/drama/problem.
cards.example: ¡Menuda movida hubo ayer en la oficina!
cards.translation: Movida is deeply tied to Spanish slang culture.

cards.front: Curro
cards.back: Literal meaning: slang work/job. Real usage: work, job, workload.
cards.translation: Informal everyday word.

cards.front: Agobiarse
cards.back: Literal meaning: to suffocate/oppress oneself. Real usage: to feel mentally overwhelmed.
cards.translation: Very emotionally expressive verb.

cards.front: Pillar
cards.back: Literal meaning: to catch/grab. Real usage: to understand/get.
cards.translation: Very versatile colloquial verb.

cards.front: Qué guay
cards.back: Literal meaning: no clear literal meaning. Real usage: cool, nice.
cards.translation: Classic Spain Spanish.

cards.front: Me mola
cards.back: Literal meaning: it cools me/pleases me (historically unclear). Real usage: I like it, it's cool.
cards.translation: Very colloquial positive opinion.

cards.front: Vas a flipar
cards.back: Literal meaning: you're going to hallucinate. Real usage: you're going to be amazed / blown away.
cards.example: Vas a flipar cuando lo veas.
cards.translation: Very expressive modern slang. Also: flipar en colores = to be totally amazed.

cards.front: Estar de bajón
cards.back: Literal meaning: to be in a downward state. Real usage: to feel emotionally low.
cards.example: Hoy estoy un poco de bajón.
cards.translation: Soft emotional expression.

cards.front: Ponerse las pilas
cards.back: Literal meaning: to put batteries into oneself. Real usage: to get motivated/start acting seriously.
cards.example: Tengo que ponerme las pilas con el español.
cards.translation: Very visual and common phrase.

cards.front: Ir a saco
cards.back: Literal meaning: to go to the sack/bag. Real usage: to go all in/full force.
cards.example: Esta semana voy a saco con AWS.
cards.translation: Strong energy/focus expression.

cards.front: Estar al loro
cards.back: Literal meaning: to be at the parrot. Real usage: to pay attention/stay alert.
cards.example: Estate al loro con ese correo.
cards.translation: Funny old-school Spain expression.
